subject: Clarify default capture window for requests, prompts, and generated outputs
messages:
From: Sophie Lemaire <sophie.lemaire@novatek.io>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Novatek Security Team <security@novatek.io>
Date: 2028-07-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on what you keep by default (prompts vs outputs)

Hi Diego,

Quick follow-up from our security checklist review — we need to confirm Redwood's default behavior for captured data so we can sign off internally. Specific asks:

- By default, does Redwood persist full request payloads (user prompt + system prompt) and the model-generated outputs, or just metadata? If retained, what are the default retention durations for each?
- Are model outputs (the generated response) considered \"logs\" or \"artifacts\" for the purposes of deletion requests?
- For EU-hosted accounts, is the persisted data kept in EU-only storage by default?
- What is the timeline and mechanism for a customer-initiated deletion (API or support ticket)? SLA for complete purge?

We are trying to map this to our retention policy (13 months max, with some automated purge windows). Any concise, authoritative statement you can provide — preferably with steps we can include in our internal SOC pack — would be hugely helpful.

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Lemaire
Security Engineer — Novatek

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lemaire <sophie.lemaire@novatek.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-05T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on what you keep by default (prompts vs outputs)

Sophie — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (policy/ops) and Rishi (infra) so you get the precise answers and the purge/playbook. Attaching a short summary PDF that covers the default behavior and deletion options.

High level from sales/AE side:
- Default platform capture includes request metadata (timestamps, model id, routing decisions) for 90 days.
- Full payload capture (prompts + generated outputs) is enabled by default for new hosted accounts but retained only for 30 days unless the customer opts into longer analytics retention.
- EU accounts can be configured to store persisted captures in EU regions only (we do this by default for customers who sign up through our EU partner flow).
- Customers can request deletion via the DataDelete API or through a support ticket; standard path kicks off a purge job we aim to complete within 72 hours. Marissa/Rishi: please confirm exact SLAs and tombstone/audit behavior.

Short attachment: retention_summary_v1.pdf

Next steps: Marissa — can you confirm the hard guarantees (and whether tombstones remain for billing/audit), and Rishi — please add technical details about streaming/caching and backup snapshots.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lemaire <sophie.lemaire@novatek.io>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-05T14:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on what you keep by default (prompts vs outputs)

Sophie — adding a concise, policy-grade answer you can drop into your SOC pack. I keep this intentionally operational and prescriptive.

Summary (authoritative):
1) Classification:
   - Request metadata: routing headers, timestamps, model_id, token counts. Persisted by default as operational telemetry.
   - Prompts (input payloads) and generated outputs (model responses): treated as customer artifacts. They are captured by default for hosted accounts to support debugging, evals, and quality monitoring.

2) Default retention windows (hosted):
   - Request metadata: 90 days.
   - Prompts + generated outputs (full payloads): 30 days by default, then purged from primary storage.
   - Short-lived caches (KV cache, streaming buffers): ephemeral (kept < 24 hours) and not part of persisted logs.

3) EU residency:
   - For customers that sign up in the EU or request EU residency, persisted captures are placed on EU-only storage by default. Please note: backups/snapshots that cross regions are only used for disaster recovery under strict access controls and are retained for a short window (see infra note below).

4) Deletion mechanics & SLA:
   - DataDelete API: customer calls initiate a queued purge job. We aim to remove payloads from primary indexes within 72 hours.
   - Secondary/backups: retained up to 7 days for disaster recovery; during that window data may persist in immutable snapshots and be purged according to the DR retention schedule.
   - Audit/tombstone records: after purge, an immutable audit record (minimal metadata: deletion request id, timestamp) is retained for 13 months to satisfy compliance and billing reconciliation. The audit record does not contain prompt or output contents.

5) PII handling & recommended customer actions:
   - Redwood does not perform automatic PII redaction by default. For sensitive workloads we recommend: client-side pseudonymization, request-side prompt redaction hooks, or enabling our \"no-persist\" mode for specific routes.

6) Exceptions & legal holds:
   - Legal or regulatory holds can delay purges; those are handled via our enterprise support flow. If a legal hold is asserted, affected records are flagged and retained until the hold is released.

I'll attach a one-page playbook (delete-playbook.md) that lists the exact API calls, required headers, and the internal on-call steps we take when a deletion request is received. Rishi: please confirm the backup snapshot windows below so we can pass exact numbers to Sophie.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Policy — Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lemaire <sophie.lemaire@novatek.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-06T16:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on what you keep by default (prompts vs outputs)

Hi Sophie — quick technical clarifications to Marissa's policy summary so your ops/security team has the exact flows:

- Streaming tokens: generated tokens emitted over a stream are not persisted in a long-term store unless capture is explicitly enabled at the request layer.
- KV cache & session caches: these are in-memory by default, flushed at session end, and never written to the long-term log store unless capture is requested.
- Primary persistence: when full payload capture is enabled, we write the request and response objects to our log store; those records are then subject to the 30-day purge job Marissa referenced.
- Backups & DR: production snapshots are created for DR and retained for 7 days. Snapshot retention is application-level and encrypted; during that 7-day window content may remain until the snapshot lifecycle job rotates them out. We do not replicate EU data to non-EU regions for EU-residency customers (except under explicit customer consent).
- Deletion implementation: DataDelete API enqueues a job that marks records for removal, removes them from primary indexes, and then a separate compaction job truncates underlying storage blocks. The whole flow (enqueue -> index removal -> compaction) is usually complete within 72 hours; compaction timing can vary slightly under heavy load but support tickets will list the purge job id for audit.

If Novatek wants an even tighter window or zero-capture routes, we can propose a configuration change in the Dedicated plan or use per-route no-persist policies. Happy to set up a short technical session to walk your engineers through implementation patterns.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
